items.title: Louis Cottrell, Jr. Interview, 1961-08-25
items.q: Tubby Hall, that's right. Yeah, Tubby Hall, I can remember.

ctx.x: And if they didn't, I'm going to say quite a few of them, maybe like Baby Dodds even, who went to Chicago. I think he only had a few lessons. He wouldn't tell us too much about it. I think your father didn't get along too well with him. He didn't learn to read fast enough or something. Well, it could have been that. He was kind of impatient. I'll tell you that. That was one thing why I didn't want to learn how to play a drum. Because he was a little impatient. Even if they only took a few lessons, there's maybe…

Because you take a few of the old times that's still living, like, Happy Goldstein, he always remarked to me what a wonderful father my father was, and the way he used to admire walking behind him, second line, just to hear him play. And so many of the other boys. You take like the two minor boys, I can remember faintly them coming over to them. That was minor hall, I mean the two hall boys, and Baby Hall. In Tubby Hall, yeah. Tubby Hall, that's right. Yeah, Tubby Hall, I can remember.

I knew both of them quite well, one in Chicago and the other in Los Angeles. Yes. Both dead now. They are. Minor Hall just died about a year ago. Just about. Yeah, but just about everybody I ever talked to mentioned your father, I guess, from here. Any drummer and others too. Is there anything else you can tell us about his drum set? Well, I think that as far as cymbals or wood blocks or the hall bells, what else did he use?
